patch.value: Nested pm test coverage changes repository-root fixtures because outer PM_PATH sandboxing leaks into package-owned run-tests

Running node scripts/run-tests.mjs coverage directly from the checkout passes all 381 files and 6,451 tests at 100/100/100/100. Linking the identical command through pm test fails 11 validate ownership/path-classification cases under schema context and the same cases plus merge-receipt context under tracker context. The outer linked-test runner replaces PM_PATH with a temporary schema or tracker copy; repository-root validation fixtures then derive ownership and path candidates from the copied tracker rather than the checkout, despite run-tests.mjs providing its own inner test sandboxes. This makes the documented package-owned sandbox runner unsafe to compose as a broad linked test and produces false product failures.

Direct and pm-linked executions of node scripts/run-tests.mjs coverage produce the same test and coverage result; No unit or integration test reads or writes the real repository .agents/pm tracker; Schema and tracker linked-test modes retain their documented semantics for genuine pm commands
Make package-owned test runners compositionally isolated when invoked through pm linked-test sandboxes
The same authoritative coverage command should have one result whether run directly or through PM evidence orchestration
Prevents false coverage failures and lets broad gates be recorded as executable PM evidence without exposing the real tracker
run-tests.mjs derives repository fixtures from the checkout while every test PM read/write remains sandboxed, and a nested pm test regression proves parity
PR #795 exact-head verification produced repeatable direct-green/linked-red evidence in both schema and tracker modes
Package-owned coverage remains 100/100/100/100 under a linked PM run without repository-root fixture drift
Direct coverage is green; schema and tracker linked contexts alter PM_PATH-derived ownership and path scans and fail otherwise-green tests
